issues.description: The Rideable.messageOnRide method has a parameter in the solution but is specified without parameters in the problem statement and is used without parameters in the template. The problem statement/UML and the template expect messageOnRide():String (no arguments) and instruct students to implement a return like "Riding on [Animal Type] [name]". In the solution repository, Rideable.messageOnRide is declared as messageOnRide(String equipment) and Pig/Seal implement that signature, returning strings that include the equipment (e.g. "Riding on Pig [name] with [equipment]"). This parameter mismatch is structural: students following the problem and template will implement a no-arg method and/or call messageOnRide() with no argument (as shown in template Main), which will not match the solution's interface and will cause compile errors or confusion about the intended API and return value format.
issues.suggested_fix:
Make the Rideable API consistent across artifacts. Two viable fixes (choose one based on intended teaching goal):

1) Align the solution to the problem/template (recommended): Change Rideable.messageOnRide to the no-argument signature (String messageOnRide()) and update Pig and Seal to implement messageOnRide() returning exactly the format described in the statement (e.g. "Riding on Pig [name]"). Also update any solution tests or usages expecting the equipment parameter.

2) If the intent is to include an equipment parameter, update the problem statement and the template Main usage to document and call messageOnRide(String equipment). Adjust the textual specification (replace messageOnRide() with messageOnRide(String equipment) and update the expected return format) so students implement the same signature as the solution.

Either approach resolves the structural mismatch; prefer (1) unless the exercise was intentionally meant to teach parameterized interface methods.

issues.description: The problem statement and the template expect a zero-argument Rideable.messageOnRide() that returns a String like "Riding on [Animal Type] [name]" (UML and explicit text). The solution repository defines Rideable.messageOnRide(String equipment) (adds a parameter) and implements Pig/Seal accordingly (returning strings that include "with [equipment]"). This changes the method signature and the expected return format, causing a mapping mismatch: students reading the problem/template will implement/expect messageOnRide() with no parameters, but the solution uses a different API. This discrepancy is likely unintentional and forces students to reconcile two different method signatures for the same conceptual action (ride an animal).
issues.suggested_fix: Align the solution with the problem/template by changing the Rideable interface and its implementations to the zero-argument signature expected by the exercise: declare String messageOnRide(); then update Pig and Seal to implement messageOnRide() with no parameters and return exactly "Riding on [Animal Type] [name]" (e.g. "Riding on Pig Doodle"). Alternatively, if the equipment parameter is deliberate, update the problem statement and template to document the parameter and the expected return format consistently — but prefer changing the solution to match the exercise text/template.
